storage_audit.measurement_method: Real PostgreSQL 15 instance (Docker, local), NOT estimated from CSV file size. Measured via pg_database_size() and pg_total_relation_size() after running the full migration + seed + import + ML training pipeline end to end.
storage_audit.decision: PRESERVE ALL DATA -- NO OPTIMIZATION PERFORMED. The measured PostgreSQL footprint (44.17 MB) uses only ~11% of the 400MB target budget and ~9% of the 500MB hard limit. Per the data-preservation rule (never destroy useful historical data to hit a storage number when the data already comfortably fits), column removal, deduplication, data-type optimization, and temporal downsampling were all evaluated and explicitly skipped as unnecessary. Every dataset is imported at its full originally-validated resolution, column set, and date range -- unchanged from the original import.

weather.notes: ERA5 reanalysis via Open-Meteo; fully populated for every downloaded year (2018-2025). A 6-year window is imported.
weather.reason_for_no_reduction: Dataset already comfortably fits the free-tier storage budget (44.17 MB actual measured PostgreSQL total vs. 400 MB target / 500 MB hard limit); no reduction needed or performed.

air_quality.exclusion_reason: 2018-2021 have 0% AQI coverage in the downloaded CAMS reanalysis data; 2022 has only ~41% coverage (3,571/8,760 hours). Importing partial years would misrepresent them as complete, so only the fully-populated years are loaded.
air_quality.reason_for_no_reduction: Dataset already comfortably fits the free-tier storage budget (44.17 MB actual measured PostgreSQL total vs. 400 MB target / 500 MB hard limit); the years excluded above were excluded for data-quality reasons (incomplete coverage), not for storage reasons.

marine.notes: Wave height/direction/period are populated from 2022 onward. sea_surface_temp_c and sea_level_height_msl_m are partially null in 2022-2023 (Open-Meteo Marine API backfill limitation) -- imported as NULL, not fabricated.
marine.reason_for_no_reduction: Dataset already comfortably fits the free-tier storage budget (44.17 MB actual measured PostgreSQL total vs. 400 MB target / 500 MB hard limit); no reduction needed or performed.

port_traffic.notes: Annual aggregate statistics only (Indian Ports Association / port authority reports). Deliberately NOT used to derive any daily/hourly figure -- too coarse for that.
port_traffic.reason_for_no_reduction: Dataset already comfortably fits the free-tier storage budget; annual aggregate table is negligibly small regardless.
